# Threat Actor Profile

Type 7 · Analytical and attribution · `threat-actor-profile` · ID prefix `PG-TAP-`

A maintained reference on one actor: who it is, what it wants, whom it targets, how its operations have changed, what it uses, how its infrastructure behaves, and which techniques it uses.

**Use it when:** An actor recurs in investigations or is named in a requirement. Reissue it as the dossier grows; the revision history records each change.

| | |
|---|---|
| Audience | CTI analysts, Threat hunters, Security leadership |
| Tier | Strategic |
| Default marking | TLP:AMBER · PAP:AMBER |
| Valid for | 180 days from issue |
| Formats | markdown, json, stix |
| Suggested for PIRs | Threat actor and campaign tracking (strategic) |

## Sections

In order. A required section with no content makes the report **Incomplete**, and the report names it. Every report has the header, the PIR verdict, Gaps and Limitations, and Sources.

| # | Section | Required | Provenance | Built from |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Report header (`header`) | yes | Method | ReportIssue, reports/contract.py |
| 2 | Priority intelligence requirement (`pir_verdict`) | yes | Method | AnalyticInvestigation, reports/pir.py |
| 3 | Actor identity (`actor_identity`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (alias, mitre-group, origin) |
| 4 | Key judgments (`key_judgments`) | yes | Analyst + Model draft | analytic ledger assertions and hypotheses |
| 5 | Motivation and objectives (`motivation`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (motivation) |
| 6 | Victimology (`victimology`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (targets-sector, targets-region) |
| 7 | Historical timeline (`historical_timeline`) | yes | Evidence | actor claims (campaign), observations |
| 8 | Arsenal and tooling (`arsenal`) | yes | Evidence + Analyst | actor claims (uses-malware, uses-tool), file observations |
| 9 | Infrastructure and OPSEC patterns (`infra_opsec`) | yes | Evidence + Method | STIX objects |
| 10 | ATT&CK techniques and procedures (`attack_matrix`) | yes | Evidence | accepted framework mappings, pinned ATT&CK Enterprise v19.2 |
| 11 | Gaps and limitations (`gaps_limitations`) | yes | Method + Analyst | lifecycle knowledge_gap and limitation items, element results |
| 12 | Sources (`sources`) | yes | Method | module runs |

## What each section must say

- **Report header.** Report ID, version, status, marking, audience, requirement, validity and producer.
- **Priority intelligence requirement.** The question, its category and tier, and the deterministic verdict (DEC-PIR-001).
- **Actor identity.** The tracked name, every alias with who uses it, the MITRE group ID when one exists, and any origin or sponsorship assessment stated as a judgment.
- **Key judgments.** Origin or sponsorship, objectives and expected next activity, each with likelihood, separate confidence and basis.
- **Motivation and objectives.** financial, espionage, disruption, ideology or other; the statement gives the basis.
- **Victimology.** Targeted sectors and regions, each with its basis and citations.
- **Historical timeline.** Dated campaigns, tooling changes and disruptions, oldest first, each with a citation.
- **Arsenal and tooling.** Malware families and dual-use tools attributed by claim, and the files collected.
- **Infrastructure and OPSEC patterns.** Attributes shared by two or more collected objects (TLD, registrar, name server, ASN, hosting, certificate issuer), with how often each was seen.
- **ATT&CK techniques and procedures.** Tactic, technique ID and name, and the observed procedure, from accepted mappings against the pinned release.
- **Gaps and limitations.** Recorded knowledge gaps and limitations, plus every element that came back empty or partial.
- **Sources.** Every collection source that ran, with run and object counts and its Admiralty rating.

## Rules every report follows

- Indicator values are defanged in Markdown and unchanged in JSON, STIX and rule files.
- Each judgment states a likelihood term and, separately, a confidence level ([vocabularies](README.md#vocabularies)).
- Each section shows its provenance; each source shows its Admiralty rating.
- Examples use reserved names and addresses only (RFC 2606, RFC 5737, RFC 3849).
